rows: Drats. It doth seem fated that I shant catch anything.
The most befuddling bit is I shant ascertain if it is due to improper location, or time.
Let's head back, Scarlet.
A little bit longer, I beg of thee.
I shall catch a most prodigious specimen, I'm sure of it.
That's what you've been saying for the past four hours.
And the rain is starting to really come down.
Dost thou now be aware?
With heavy precipitation, thy chance of angling a sizeable fish thus increases.
It also increases your chances of getting into an accident.
Please, heed my beseechment. Just a bit longer. Thy desire to feast upon maritime creatures is what initially led us on this venture.
If we rush, something is bound to go afoul.
Are you sure it's not something to do with what you're using as a rod?
Is a scabbard meant to be used like that?
Not only that, but it will be thankful to me for being able to serve a purpose other than that intended of a scabbard.
In these times that we live in, scabbards are not often of much use,
for our swords are more often than not being brandished outside of them.
... Come again?
A scabbard is only of use if thy blade is not being used.
Yet, in these war-torn times, I am forever swinging my blade to and fro.
But if your sword is always out of its sheath, other people could get hurt.
Hmm?
You're quite skilled, so it shouldn't be too much of a problem, but not everyone is as skilled as you are.
Innocent bystanders could be walking past and accidentally get cut if everyone had their swords out in the open.
It's very dangerous, you know. Safety precautions need to be taken with every type of weapon.
Not to mention that constantly having a sword unsheathed would negatively affect its lifespan.
... Fair enough.
Very well, I shall desist from using my scabbard as a fishing rod.
You have made a fine point, and I can see how this could be a dangerous act.
A wise decision.
I feel something biting! It's a big one!
Oh my gosh!
What a brilliant way to end the day!
Let us wrap up our venture in a grand fashion!
